FOREWORD

0.1 Thil Indian Standard (Part 3) (First Revision)

adopted

_by the Indian Standards Institution on 5 February 1985, after the draft finalized by the Fertilizers Sectional Committee had been approved by

the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1971. Giving due consideration to the views of manufacturers, testing authorities and the technologists, the concerned Committee decided to revise this standard and felt that the methods of test should be related to those currently used in the . induatriallaboratories. 0.3 Earlier, only the 'gravimetric quinolinium molybdophosphate method" had been specified for the determination of phosphorus. The present revision includes, as alternatives, 'alkalimetric quinolinium molybdophoaphate method' and 'spectrophotometric moJybdo-vanado phosphate method' both of which are widely used in laboratories dealiug with phosphatic fertilizers. The gravimetric method ii, however, to be used as the referee method in ~ae of any dispute.

O.t In the preparation of this standard, consideration haa a)1O been given
to the need for maintaining co-ordination with the methods for sampling and test for fertilizers prelcribed under the F",Uior ( Conl,ol) O,tl", 1957 and 'hi &1111'"" CDmmodiliu Act, 1955 (Incorporating amendment up to August 1981 ), of the Government of India. 0.5 In the preparation of this standard, considerable ..siltance hal been derived from the following pubUcatioDS: Official methods of analyail. The A��ociation of Official Analytical Chemists, Washington DC, USA. 1978. Recommended analytical method.. The National Plant Food Institute, Washington DC, USA. 3

IS IAn (Pan 3) �1985
The Fertilizers and feeding stuff regulations 1960. Department of Agriculture, UK.

0.6 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off. it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960��

6.3.2 Proe,du"

6.3.2.2 Transfer an aliquot of the sample solution cootaining 20 to 30 mg of P,O, and Dot more than 5 ml of concentrated acid, to 500-ml conical flask, add 20 ml of 10 percent citric acid solution, and adjust to about 100 mi. Add 60 of quimociac reagent, immediately cover with watch glass, and place on medium temperature hot plate. After the solution comes to boiling point, move to cooler portion of hot plate and boil gently for one minute. Let it cool until ftuk can be handled comfortably with bare hand. Allow the precipitate to aettle down.
6.3.2~3 Prepare a uniform pulped-paper pad about .5 mm thick on perforated porcelain disc in a funnel ( 60� ) fitted on a suction flask by adding not leu than 2 approximately equal incrementa of water suspension of pulped paper and suckinl dry with vacuum between additions. Ensure that the setting is leakproof. Swirl the flask, pour contents on to the filter and' wash the flask five times with 15 ml portions of water adding washings to funnel. Immediately after funnel has emptied, wash down sides with about 15 mJ of water to remove residual acetone, which causes excessively fast drying and later lump formation jf allowed to evaporate, Wash with 3 additional 15 ml portions of water, letting funnel empty between additions. En.ure that no free acid is left ( precipitate should be washed acid free). Keep drying of precipitate to minimum. Using only a jet of water. transfer the precipitate and pad to precipitatioD flask and break up the pad with a jet ~r water. Do not smear the precipitate against the funnel or fluk.

6.3.2.t DiIIolve the precipitate by funning down standard sodium hydroxide solution in amall loti from a burette and add 3 to 5 ml in excess. Add I ml of mised iadicator and titrate with standard nitric acid solution to greyish blue end point. If overtitrated ( greenish-yellow) add additional excess standard sodium hydroxide lolution and re-titrate to greyish-blue.
